payload.summary: Five amendments should be accepted as real conservation or budget-tracking issues. The CleanFilter routing amendment should be rejected because filter cleaning is documented as an intentional export, not an in-tank recycling path.

votes.rationale: TrimPlants currently adds raw plant biomass grams directly to fine_detritus_g_total in engine.rs, but the budget interprets detritus grams with the detrital organic stoichiometry, not plant stoichiometry. That inflates both nitrogen and carbon relative to the removed plant biomass. Senescence already uses plant_detrital_mass_g for this conversion, so the trim path is inconsistent and should be brought into line; the exact patch may need exposing or reusing that helper.

docs/ROUTING.md explicitly defines CleanFilter as a maintenance export: removed fouling leaves the tank, and no new detritus pool is created during cleaning. The current action already reduces in-tank biomass, which is the intended export semantics, and budget tracking can represent that as an outflow on the action stage. Routing the removed microbial biomass into DON/DOC would contradict the documented behavior by keeping exported waste inside the tank.

mortality() in shrimp.rs reduces adult and juvenile counts without moving the dead biomass into any other pool. total_nitrogen() and total_carbon() both include shrimp biomass via the count-based helpers, so deaths currently remove N and C from the model. docs/ROUTING.md also explicitly says shrimp death should route to fine_detritus_g_total and calls shrimp mortality out as an implementation gap.

The conservation tests use active_budget_state(), which hard-codes zero adults and zero juveniles, so they never exercise shrimp lifecycle or mortality paths. That leaves a real blind spot around one of the known conservation gaps. A seeded variant with live shrimp is an appropriate guardrail, though the setup should ensure the mortality path is actually exercised deterministically.

ElementBudget::from_delta derives in_mg and out_mg from a single net before/after delta. That loses gross source and sink information for stages that both remove and add the same element within one pass, such as water changes with non-zero replacement chemistry or dissolved oxygen updates with simultaneous reaeration/photosynthesis and respiration. Net conservation checks still work, but the per-stage ledger does not faithfully record sources and sinks as described by the budget-tracking contract.

The guardrail test only compares budget labels against numeric state paths that first pass through hard-coded nitrogen/carbon allowlists. If a new element-bearing field is added to TankState and the allowlist is not updated, that field is excluded from the comparison entirely and the test still passes. That means the test does not actually force future contributors to extend total_nitrogen() or total_carbon() when new explicit pools are introduced.
